The gf (also on Voat) and I decided to go to Myrtle Beach, SC for small weekend getaway. We leave a great bar at 11:56 (The Chemist, highly recommended btw - modern drinks and great whiskey selection) and decide to walk north on the boardwalk. We then hear 5 pops that sound bit like distant fire crackers. We (heading north at about 8th ave and ocean) both turn around looking for fireworks of some sort, but there is nothing, so we keep walking (there was no screaming or panic or anything either that would indicate anything strange). All is silent for a few minutes as we head back.

By the time we reach 9th and Chesters, we hear a chorus of sirens. We see a police golf cart go by, then a police SUV, then a police minivan (we are marveling at the diversity of their police vehicles), and then it dawns first on my girlfriend and she asks if that could have been a shooting. We (and everyone else) intently look on, as a full column of police vehicles are rushing down Ocean blvd and King's hwy - they fan out with a group of police vehicles taking every road and alleyway towards 6th ave (the execution of which was really cool to watch). The rear vehicles in the column block traffic - they set up a perimeter bounded by 7th and King's.

We run to the car (as we are hoping to grab some pictures for you Goats before they shut the whole place down) and manage to sneak down 6th just behind an ambulance and moments before a fire truck arrives behind us (which blocked the entrance from King's). All entrances onto Ocean's are already blocked, and so we are forced to turn onto Flagg.

Please pardon the quality as I couldn't really give my GF time to set up good shots.

Facing south on 7th toward Ocean blvd, less than 2 minutes after they started shutting things down.

Same position a few seconds later, just before we decided to U-turn (more units showing up).

On Flagg, facing south towards 5th. This photo doesn't properly convey the level of activity - there is another ambulance visible on the right, and loads of police both in front and behind, heading down 4th towards Ocean.

On Flagg, vehicle facing north towards 5th, camera facing towards Ocean. This is the first ambulance on site, and is apparently the location of the shooting. The building on the left is a Budget Inn - everyone and their kid is out on the balcony looking. I chatted up a few of them from the car window for details.

So, time for lessons learned and strange notes:

  • I have been raised around firearms, even shooting competition as a kid. I have heard all manner of exotic firearms, yet when hearing the gunshots a literal 900 ft away from me, I didn't perceive them to be gunshots (and neither did anyone else). It was only the massive police response that tipped us off. There was no panic, no reaction from the crowd either that would have tipped us off.

  • Because of the extremely loud vehicles (both engines and sound systems) on Ocean's, you likely wouldn't have even heard the gunshots if you were just one more block further away than where we were (which is well within range of a stray bullet).

  • We usually walk both ends of the boardwalk. Because of the strange way the universe works, we decided not to this time on what truly felt like a whim. Trust your instincts.

  • Also for weird reasons, at some random point I felt compelled to ask our bartender at The Chemist about crime in the area (I usually prefer lighter conversation). The girl leans over and lowers her voice to tell me that it is actually really bad, and that the police work really hard to cover it up because of tourism. She tells me there was a shooting just this afternoon, and that if we look closely, there are always a ton of police hiding everywhere on the strip while remaining mostly out of sight (we have noticed cruisers sitting in the trash corrals besides the massive dumpsters, bike cops tucked away on very small alleys between buildings, etc). She finally tells me that everyone who knows the area goes somewhere else for nightlife/bars/food/etc. [I forgot where she said, but will update it if I remember]

  • It was hard to tell with all of the excitement of trying to find a way INTO their perimeter before they closed it off, but we think we heard a second series of shots while we were in the car. We think that the second shots may have been the police vs the shooter, and the second ambulance on 4th was for the shooter.

  • Heading north on 17 toward north Myrtle we passed the hospital where the ambulances were dropping the victims off.

  • I have been shilling getting a CCH permit to my gf for a long time, this was the tipping point for her.
